Figure 2: RIG-I-only vs STAT-only signatures in influenza-infected A549 cells (scRNA-Seq)

Carlos Ramirez

2026-10-27 17:03:58

This markdown reproduces the panels of Figure 2. We project the RIG-I-only and STAT-only (IFN-only) signatures, derived from the A549 bulk model in Figure 1, onto single-cell RNA-Seq data of A549 cells infected with influenza A virus (H3N2) over a time course (uninfected, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 h post infection; Rivera et al. 2025, GSE287024). Every cell is scored with both signatures (Seurat AddModuleScore), and cells are classified into two quadrants of the RIG-I-only vs STAT-only score plane:

  • Quadrant I: high RIG-I-only score and low STAT-only score (rigi_only >= 0.1 and stat_only <= 0.05), i.e. cells with direct RIG-I activity but no IFN-receptor signalling.
  • Quadrant II: high STAT-only score and low RIG-I-only score (stat_only >= 0.05 and rigi_only < 0), i.e. bystander cells responding to secreted IFN.

Panels produced (all saved in figures/figure_02/):

Panel file Content
a549_quadrantes_across_time_rivera.pdf RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores per time point, coloured by quadrant
barplot_prop_quadrants_rivera.pdf Proportion of all cells falling in quadrant I / II per time point
quantification_interferon_expression_rivera.pdf IFNB1, IFNL1 and IFNL2 expression in quadrant I vs II cells per time point (Wilcoxon test)
oasl_ifnl1_ha_rigi_vs_stat.pdf RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of infected cells coloured by IFNL1, OASL and viral HA expression
oasl_vs_rigi.pdf Viral HA expression vs OASL expression / RIG-I-only score, coloured and sized by IFNL1

The code was taken from the original analysis script /media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/july_2026/02_scRNASeq_projections_Rivera.Rmd keeping only what is needed for these panels; plotting code, PDF sizes and aesthetics are unchanged.

  prefix = c(
    "GSM8736732_Uninfected",
    "GSM8736733_Infected_8hrs_1",
    "GSM8736734_Infected_8hrs_2",
    "GSM8736735_Infected_10hrs_1",
    "GSM8736736_Infected_10hrs_2",

Raw-data processing (not evaluated)

The next three chunks document how the cached Seurat object was built from the raw 10x matrices: one Seurat object per sample (cells with at least 3000 detected genes), sample annotation added to the metadata, merging, log-normalisation, scaling, PCA and UMAP. They are not evaluated (eval = FALSE; the original guarded them with reprocess/rerun = FALSE) because the processing is slow and its result is stored in a549_iav_rivera_scRNASeq.rds, which is loaded below. Note that the saving step would write into the data folder; it must not be run from this repository without changing the output path.

path <- path2rivera

if ( reprocess == TRUE ){
          seurat_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(samples)), function(i) {

          counts <- ReadMtx(
            mtx = file.path(path, paste0(samples$prefix[i], "_matrix.mtx.gz")),
            features = file.path(path, paste0(samples$prefix[i], "_features.tsv.gz")),
            cells = file.path(path, paste0(samples$prefix[i], "_barcodes.tsv.gz"))
          )

          obj <- CreateSeuratObject(
            counts = counts,
            project = samples$sample_id[i],
            min.cells = 0,
            min.features = 3000
          )

          # Add metadata
          obj$sample     <- samples$sample_id[i]
          obj$condition  <- ifelse(str_detect(samples$sample_id[i], "Uninfected"),
                                   "Uninfected", "Infected")
          obj$timepoint  <- str_extract(samples$sample_id[i], "\\d+h")
          obj$replicate  <- str_extract(samples$sample_id[i], "_\\d$")

          return(obj)
        })

        names(seurat_list) <- samples$sample_id
}

Merging the per-sample Seurat objects.

if ( reprocess == TRUE ) {
       merged_obj <- merge(
  x = seurat_list[[1]],
  y = seurat_list[-1],
  add.cell.ids = names(seurat_list),
  project = "Rivera_concat"
)
merged_obj

rm(seurat_list)
}

Standard pre-processing and saving of the cached object.

if ( rerun == TRUE ) {
        DefaultAssay(merged_obj) <- "RNA"
        merged_obj <- NormalizeData(merged_obj, verbose = FALSE)
        merged_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(merged_obj,
                                   nfeatures = 20000)
        merged_obj <- ScaleData(merged_obj, verbose = FALSE)
        merged_obj <- RunPCA(merged_obj, npcs = 50)
        merged_obj <- RunUMAP(merged_obj, dims = 1:49, verbose = FALSE)

        saveRDS(merged_obj,
                file = paste0(path2rivera,
                              "/a549_iav_rivera_scRNASeq.rds"),
                compress = TRUE)
}

Score columns already stored in the cached object (if any). They are kept aside to compare with the scores recomputed below.

cached_score_cols <- intersect(c("stat_only1", "rigi_only2"),
                               colnames(merged_obj@meta.data))
cached_score_cols
## [1] "stat_only1" "rigi_only2"
cached_scores <- merged_obj@meta.data[, cached_score_cols, drop = FALSE]

Scoring cells with the RIG-I-only / STAT-only signatures

Loading signatures

Signatures from Figure 1 (path2signs). As in the original analysis, genes whose symbol contains “IFN” are removed (to avoid scoring the interferon transcripts themselves, which are later used as read-outs) and the list is re-ordered to stat_only, rigi_only. Because of this order, AddModuleScore names the score columns stat_only1 and rigi_only2.

signatures <- readRDS(path2signs)
signatures <- lapply(signatures,
                     function(genes){
                             grep(pattern = 'IFN',
                                  x = genes,
                                  value = TRUE,
                                  invert = TRUE)
                     })
signatures <- signatures[c(2, 1)]
str(signatures)
## List of 2
##  $ stat_only: chr [1:99] "PNPT1" "TRIM5" "CSF1" "ZNF711" ...
##  $ rigi_only: chr [1:94] "EGR4" "CXCL11" "FOSB" "EGR2" ...

Scoring cells

Module scores with Seurat AddModuleScore (default seed = 1, hence deterministic).

merged_obj <- AddModuleScore(
  object = merged_obj,
  features = signatures,
  name = names(signatures)
)

Comparison of recomputed scores with those stored in the cached object (only if the cached object contained score columns).

if (length(cached_score_cols) > 0) {
        for (sc in cached_score_cols) {
                d <- merged_obj@meta.data[rownames(cached_scores), sc] -
                        cached_scores[[sc]]
                cat(sc, ": max |recomputed - cached| =",
                    max(abs(d), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
        }
} else {
        cat("The cached object does not contain stat_only1 / rigi_only2 scores;",
            "scores are computed here only.\n")
}
## stat_only1 : max |recomputed - cached| = 0 
## rigi_only2 : max |recomputed - cached| = 0

Extracting scores and expression values

Cell metadata with a discrete time-point factor (uninfected cells = Control) plus the log-normalised expression of IFNL1, IFNL2, IFNB1, OASL and the viral haemagglutinin (HA) transcript.

md <- merged_obj@meta.data
md$'time_discrete' <- md$timepoint
md$'time_discrete'[is.na(md$'time_discrete')] <- 'Control'
md$'time_discrete' <- factor(md$'time_discrete',
                             levels = c('Control', '8h', '10h',
                                        '12h', '14h', '16h'))

df <- FetchData(merged_obj, vars = c('IFNL1', 'HA', 'OASL',
                                     'IFNB1', 'IFNL2'))
all(rownames(df) == colnames(merged_obj))
## [1] TRUE
md$'IFNL1' <- df$IFNL1
md$'IFNB1' <- df$IFNB1
md$'IFNL2' <- df$IFNL2
md$'HA' <- df$HA
md$'OASL' <- df$OASL

Quadrant classification (panel a549_quadrantes_across_time_rivera.pdf)

Cells are assigned to quadrant I (stat_only1 <= 0.05 and rigi_only2 >= 0.1) or quadrant II (stat_only1 >= 0.05 and rigi_only2 < 0); all other cells are NA. The scatter plot shows the two scores per time point coloured by quadrant.

md$quadrant_q <- with(md,
  ifelse(stat_only1 <= 0.05 & rigi_only2 >= 0.1, "I",
  ifelse(stat_only1 >= 0.05 & rigi_only2 < -0.0, "II", NA))
)

cols <- brewer.pal(4, "Set2")[2:4]
names(cols) <- c("I", "II")

f1 <- ggplot(md, aes(x = rigi_only2, y = stat_only1,
               color = quadrant_q)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
        facet_wrap(~time_discrete) +
        scale_color_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(
    x = "RIGI-only",
    y = "STAT-only",
    color = "Quadrant"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

f1

pdf(file = paste0(path2figures,
                  '/a549_quadrantes_across_time_rivera.pdf'),
    width=5.0, height=3.0)
f1
dev.off()
## png 
##   2

write_tsv(cell_table,

IFN expression per quadrant (panel quantification_interferon_expression_rivera.pdf)

Log expression of IFNB1, IFNL1 and IFNL2 in quadrant I vs quadrant II cells per time point; significance of I vs II within each time point by Wilcoxon test (ggpubr::stat_compare_means).

p_ifnb1 <- md %>%
        filter(!is.na(quadrant_q)) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = time_discrete,
           y = log(IFNB1+1),
           fill = quadrant_q)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
        # Add p-values (I vs II within each timepoint)
  stat_compare_means(
    aes(group = quadrant_q),
    method = "wilcox.test",
    label = 'p.signif', label.y = 1.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Log(IFNB1 expression)",
    fill = "Quadrant"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


p_ifnl1 <- md %>%
        filter(!is.na(quadrant_q)) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = time_discrete,
           y = log(IFNL1+1),
           fill = quadrant_q)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
        # Add p-values (I vs II within each timepoint)
  stat_compare_means(
    aes(group = quadrant_q),
    method = "wilcox.test",
    label = 'p.signif', label.y = 1.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Log(IFNL expression)",
    fill = "Quadrant"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +

Proportion of cells per quadrant (panel barplot_prop_quadrants_rivera.pdf)

Fraction of all cells of each time point that fall into quadrant I or quadrant II (denominator includes unassigned cells).

count_df_vs_all_cells <- md %>%
  group_by(time_discrete, quadrant_q) %>%
        summarise(n_cells=n())

prop_q_vs_all_cells_df <- count_df_vs_all_cells %>%
  group_by(time_discrete) %>%
  mutate(prop = n_cells / sum(n_cells))

write_tsv(prop_q_vs_all_cells_df,
          file = paste0(path2analysis, "/rivera_quadrant_proportions.tsv"))

barplot_prop_q_vs_all_cell <- prop_q_vs_all_cells_df %>%
        filter(!is.na(quadrant_q)) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = time_discrete,
                    y = prop,
                    fill = quadrant_q)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
        facet_wrap(~quadrant_q, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Proportion of cells",
    fill = "Quadrant"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = 'none')

pdf(file = paste0(path2figures,
                  "/barplot_prop_quadrants_rivera.pdf"),
    width=5.0, height=2.5)
barplot_prop_q_vs_all_cell
dev.off()

IFNL1, OASL and viral load on the score plane (panel oasl_ifnl1_ha_rigi_vs_stat.pdf)

Infected cells (all time points except Control) on the RIG-I-only vs STAT-only plane, coloured by IFNL1, OASL or HA (viral) expression. Cells are sorted by the colour variable so that high expressers are drawn on top.

ifnl1 <- md %>%
        filter(time_discrete!='Control') %>%
        arrange(IFNL1) %>%
        ggplot(aes(rigi_only2,
                   stat_only1,
                   colour = IFNL1)) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 1.2) +
         geom_vline(xintercept = 0, size = 1.2) +
           geom_point(size=2) +
                scale_colour_gradient2(
  low = "darkgreen",
  mid = "yellow",
  high = "red",
  midpoint = 2,
  name = "IFNL1"
  ) +
        theme_bw()

oasl <- md %>%
        filter(time_discrete!='Control') %>%
        arrange(OASL) %>%
        ggplot(aes(rigi_only2,
                   stat_only1,
                   colour = OASL)) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 1.2) +
         geom_vline(xintercept = 0, size = 1.2) +
           geom_point(size=2) +
                scale_colour_gradient2(
  low = "darkgreen",
  mid = "yellow",
  high = "red",
  midpoint = 2,
  name = "OASL"
  ) +

virus <- md %>%

Viral load vs OASL and RIG-I-only score (panel oasl_vs_rigi.pdf)

Left: HA (viral) vs OASL expression of infected OASL-expressing cells. Right: HA vs RIG-I-only score of all infected cells. Points are coloured and sized by IFNL1 expression.

oasl_vs_rigi_oasl <- md %>%
        filter(time_discrete!='Control') %>%
        filter(OASL > 0 ) %>%
        arrange(IFNL1) %>%
        ggplot(aes(OASL,HA,
                   colour = IFNL1,
                   size = IFNL1)) +
           geom_point() +
                scale_colour_gradient2(
  low = "darkgreen",
  mid = "yellow",
  high = "red",
  midpoint = 2,
  name = "IFNL1"
  ) +
        theme_bw()

oasl_vs_rigi_rigi <- md %>%
        filter(time_discrete!='Control') %>%
        arrange(IFNL1) %>%
        ggplot(aes(rigi_only2,HA,
                   colour = IFNL1,
                   size = IFNL1)) +
           geom_point() +
                scale_colour_gradient2(
  low = "darkgreen",
  mid = "yellow",
  high = "red",
  midpoint = 2,
  name = "IFNL1"
  ) +
        theme_bw()

gridExtra::grid.arrange(oasl_vs_rigi_oasl,
                        oasl_vs_rigi_rigi, ncol = 2)

pdf(file = paste0(path2figures,
                  '/oasl_vs_rigi.pdf'),
    height=3.5, width=7)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(oasl_vs_rigi_oasl,
                        oasl_vs_rigi_rigi, ncol = 2)
dev.off()
